original_description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to write, draft, plan, or outline an ebook, e-book, digital book, guide, or short non-fiction book — including Portuguese requests like 'escrever um ebook', 'criar um e-book', 'montar um livro digital', or 'quero lançar um infoproduto em formato de livro'. Trigger even when the user only describes a topic and says they want to turn it into a book, guide, or downloadable PDF/Word product, without using the word 'ebook' explicitly. This skill guides the full pipeline: defining topic/audience, researching and fact-checking real, verifiable content, building a length-correct outline (default 30-35 pages, ~8,000-10,000 words), writing chapters using storytelling and engagement techniques that keep readers turning pages, checking readability, and handing off to the docx or pdf skill for final formatted delivery. Do not use this skill for short single-page content like blog posts, emails, or social media copy — use it for book-length, multi-chapter deliverables.
best_description: Use this skill when someone wants a nonfiction digital book or guide meant to be read start to finish — ebook, e-book, digital book, livro digital, guia digital, infoproduto, workbook, lead magnet, or a bonus/gift for clients or patients — no matter the length (a 10-page bonus counts as much as a 35-page guide) and even if they never say "ebook" or "chapters." Trigger on: "write/outline a book or guide about X," "turn our best practices into an ebook for prospects," "quero lançar um infoproduto pra vender no Hotmart," "escrever um livro digital pra dar de bônus," "livro curto pra captar leads," or any topic the user wants turned into a downloadable book/guide. Covers topic/audience definition, fact-checked research, outlining, chapter-by-chapter drafting, and readability review, then hands off to docx/pdf for formatting. The test is shape, not length or price: if it wants chapters, an outline, or a cover-to-cover read, use this. Skip only single free-standing pieces — one blog post, email, social caption, slide deck, whitepaper, or one-page flyer.
